articles.title: REBUILDING THE GLOBAL TOWN SQUARE FROM SCRATCH
articles.summary: X rebuilt its web app around one server for people, search crawlers, and link previews, replacing three separate servers. On a slow connection, the first post on a profile appears in 2.7 seconds instead of more than 22 seconds, while signed-in traffic is moving over gradually by country.

articles.title: SECURING AI AGENTS: LESSONS FROM REAL-WORLD DEPLOYMENT
articles.summary: Uber secures agents with provisioning checks, runtime enforcement, and continuous testing, adding behavioral controls to traditional authorization. Scoped intents, session context, and prompt provenance help determine whether an authorized action matches the user's request, while small specialized models and parallel checks keep latency manageable.

articles.title: MODERN CSS MIGHT MAKE YOUR FRONT-END MORE COMPLEX
articles.summary: Replacing JavaScript with container queries or :has() can simplify a component while creating hidden dependencies across the application. The migration checklist covers ownership, scope, cascade, cleanup, measured performance, and maintainability so that fewer lines do not become harder behavior to debug.

articles.title: WE ALREADY KNOW HOW TO WORK WITH AGENTS
articles.summary: Companies offer a starting point for organizing agents through specialization, delegation, management layers, and escalation. Existing communication and project tools can support agent organizations, but identity, authorization, durable state, and human accountability still need to be solved.

articles.title: YOUR CODING AGENTS MADE YOU A MANAGER
articles.summary: Working effectively with coding agents depends on clear context, self-verification, early course correction, and explicit boundaries. The advice is to turn repeated corrections into shared instructions, enforce only non-negotiable requirements, and keep humans responsible for product decisions, security boundaries, and what ships.

articles.title: WRITING AS A THINKING TOOL
articles.summary: Writing externalizes thought, exposes gaps in understanding, and creates room for connections that can be missed while reading or talking to an LLM. Separate unrestricted drafting from ruthless editing, use plain language, write for yourself, and keep a regular schedule.

INK: STATE IS A PROGRAM
articles.summary: Ink is a typed language that compiles state, derived results, and atomic updates together, keeping declared relationships consistent without hand-written cache invalidation. The MIT-licensed working prototype targets JavaScript, native Rust, Rust/Wasm, and eligible WebGPU computation, with proof-checked transformations and explicitly constrained learning.

articles.title: SPEC KIT
articles.summary: Spec Kit gives coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes for building features, fixing bugs, and assessing ideas. Its extensions, presets, and workflows let teams adapt those processes to their tools and standards.

articles.title: PI-DESKTOP
articles.summary: PI-Desktop brings projects, coding agents, models, and workflows into a persistent desktop workspace built with Electron and a Rust host core. Plugins can add tools, panels, MCP servers, and background services, while the application supports switching between cloud and local models.

articles.title: WEBMCP, EXPLAINED WITH A TO-DO APP
articles.summary: A TodoMVC example exposes seven browser tools through HTML forms and JavaScript, showing how agents can operate a page without guessing which controls to click. It covers input validation, clear tool responses, untrusted content, and confirmation hints, while explaining why tool calls do not replace UI tests.

articles.title: USE NVIDIA NEMO TO TURN AGENT FAILURES INTO TESTS AND HARNESS FIXES
articles.summary: NeMo Compass mines agent traces for recurring failures, and NeMo Eval Author turns them into domain-specific tests that can validate harness changes. In a Dassault Systèmes engineering example, the loop reduced malformed tool calls from 142 to zero and improved the evaluation score by 28% with 35% fewer tool calls per run.

articles.title: JIT BITMAP TEXT RENDERING FOR MICROCONTROLLERS
articles.summary: A microcontroller text renderer generates machine code for each string and draws through a compact one-bit intermediate buffer before expanding to RGB565. Packed glyphs, overlapping font data, and instruction scheduling reduce memory pressure and rendering cost, including shrinking one font bitmap from 1,140 to 960 bytes.

articles.title: REACH 8 MILLION TECH PROFESSIONALS READING TLDR
articles.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach software developers and engineering leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities [20].

articles.title: HOW I'M FIGHTING THE AI BRAIN FRY
articles.summary: A git-backed ticket queue and a single inbox for human decisions reduce context switching by letting each task leave working memory when it returns to the queue.

articles.title: OH MY PPT
articles.summary: A local-first tool uses AI to turn presentation, lesson, or story descriptions into HTML slides.

articles.title: GITHUB'S NEW PULL REQUEST OVERVIEW
articles.summary: An opt-in preview brings merge readiness and next actions to the top of pull requests, with conversation filters and newest-first comments.

articles.summary: Modern browser APIs and AI-assisted development make rich applications easier for individuals to build and distribute.
